title: Latency drift — investigation & profiling notes
body:
Summary:

Observed a steady increase in p95/p99 decode latency for model-x-route between 2025-01-05 and 2025-01-10. Alert fired from latency-regression rule on 2025-01-10 (alert id: LRG-2025-01-10). Initial pattern: no single spike, but tail drift across multiple instances and AZs.

Primary hypothesis threads to explore (ordered by perceived likelihood):
- upstream batching change caused higher queueing for short requests (config change or rollout of new batch window)
- KV cache invalidations (prefix cache) causing more full-prefill work
- model variant/quantization change or new kernel selection (compiler/runtime change)
- infra change: CUDA / driver / NCCL update or node-level driver update rolled out in the window
- autoscaler behavior changed (pods bouncing), creating cold-start-induced higher latencies
- noisy neighbor on GPU host (unexpected multi-tenant work)

Quick triage checklist (start here every time):
1) Confirm alert scope and affected routes/models. Query: Grafana panel "Per-route p99 (7d)" and group by route+model+region.
2) Compare canary vs prod: check canary cohorts (if available) around same traffic shape.
3) Snapshot spikes vs drift: is it steady drift or discrete step? Look at 5-min and 1h rollups.
4) Collect runtime traces from one affected request (span + token-level timestamps).
5) Correlate with infra events: deploys, driver updates, cron jobs, scaling events.
6) Run short synthetic reproducer against a known-good commit and current production binary.

Grafana / PromQL snippets used during investigation:
- p99 per route (last 24h):
  - latency_p99_ms{route=~"model-x-.*"} by (route, model)
- request queue length by host:
  - sum(rate(queued_requests_total[1m])) by (instance)
- GPU utilization (per node):
  - avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percentage[5m])
- kerneltimes / decode vs prefill breakdown (if instrumented):
  - sum(rate(inference_token_time_ms_total{phase=~"prefill|decode"}[1m])) by (phase)

BigQuery / logs queries (examples we run from root account):
- aggregate per-request latency by commit tag (if we inject git SHA into request metadata):
  SELECT commit_sha, route, APPROX_QUANTILES(latency_ms, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS p95_ms
  FROM `redwood-prod.logs.requests`
  WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP("2025-01-04") AND TIMESTAMP("2025-01-11")
  GROUP BY commit_sha, route;

- find instances with increased queueing and restarts:
  SELECT instance_id, count(*) as restarts, max(queue_len) as max_queue
  FROM `redwood-prod.service.events`
  WHERE event_type = 'restart' AND timestamp > TIMESTAMP("2025-01-04")
  GROUP BY instance_id
  ORDER BY restarts DESC

Reproduction steps (local/CI perf-harness):
- baseline commit (known-good): git checkout <good-sha>
- current candidate: git checkout <prod-sha>
- run perf harness (docker) with identical seq-length distribution and concurrency: 
  ./tools/perf-harness/run.sh --model model-x --seq-dist samples/seq-dist-jan.json --concurrency 16 --duration 600 --metrics-out /tmp/out-good.json
- compare p50/p95/p99. Repeat 3 runs per commit and take median.

Bisect approach (if suspect commit range is small):
1) Identify window of deploys: look at deploy history UI and find commits between first-good and first-bad timestamps.
2) Start git bisect between good/bad SHAs and run the perf-harness script as the test driver. Treat a >6% increase in p99 as "bad".
3) When bisecting, ensure runs are on identical hardware image and GPU driver. Use pinned infra image (ami: inference-2024-12-19).
4) Log artifacts from each run (perf JSON, flamegraph SVG, nvprof output) and upload to /artifacts/perf-bisect/<sha>/

Profiler/collection commands (what we collect for each run):
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/gpu-util.csv &
- Nsight Systems sampling (5s resolution): nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys-profile --trace=cuda,cudnn ./serving-runtime --load test-config.json
- flames (py-spy for python worker): py-spy record -o flame-<sha>.svg -- python -m serving_runtime.main --perf-mode
- perf (for native C++ agents): sudo perf record -F 99 -g -- /path/to/worker && perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg

What to collect from logs:
- model compilation logs (kernel selection, quantization fallback, jit path). Look for messages like: "kernel chosen: attention_fused_v2" or "fallback to slow matmul"
- batching window size changes / batcher decisions (samples of batch sizes over time)
- KV cache hit/miss counters and eviction logs

Example runtime trace header we want (token-level timestamps):
- request_id, model, route, commit_sha, start_prefill_ms, end_prefill_ms, start_decode_ms, end_decode_ms, tokens_generated
- compute prefill_ms = end_prefill_ms - start_prefill_ms; decode_ms = end_decode_ms - start_decode_ms

Observed signals in this incident (raw notes):
- p99 increased from ~210ms -> ~310ms for model-x-route over 7 days
- prefill time shows 30% of total increase, decode unchanged for many samples
- GPU utilization did not drop significantly; utilization near previous baseline -> points to extra CPU-side work or longer prefill kernel path
- batch size distribution shifted: more requests batched at larger windows (batch sizes increased by ~1.3x median)
- one rollout (PR #456) included a change in batch aggregator heuristics and a subtle rounding bug in sample-time estimation (potential candidate)

Hypothesis refinement: batching policy change caused more aggressive waiting (to increase throughput) which created longer queueing for short, latency-sensitive requests. The change shipped in PR #456 on 2025-01-06.

Immediate mitigation options (fast):
- revert PR #456 (if can confirm via bisect) OR patch batching policy to reduce max-wait-ms for latency-tier routes
- add a per-route override rule: latency-sensitive routes use batch_timeout_ms = 3ms
- temporarily increase capacity for route to reduce queueing (autoscale faster)

Longer-term fixes / follow-ups:
- add more granular telemetry: per-request batch-enter and batch-exit timestamps; histogram of batch sizes per-route
- expose a canary knob in runtime to simulate new batcher heuristics under traffic with low-risk routing
- automated bisect pipeline: when latency-alert triggers, run a CI bisect across commits in the deploy window using the perf-harness and present top candidate PRs in alert thread
- add regression labels to PRs that touch batching, compiler, or kernel-selection code paths

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- confirm whether any driver/NCCL updates rolled during 2025-01-05..01-08 window (infra team check)
- reproduce exact batch-size distribution shift in perf-harness (TODO: instrument traffic replayer to emulate production arrival-times)
- confirm if model artifact / param changes were published within window (model registry check)

Investigation timeline (brief):
- 2025-01-10 09:18 - Alert LRG-2025-01-10 fired (pager)
- 2025-01-10 09:30 - initial signal analysis (Miguel): p99 drift across regions, not single node
- 2025-01-10 10:45 - identified PR456 as coincident deploy on 2025-01-06
- 2025-01-12 14:22 - perf-harness runs: good-sha vs prod-sha show ~18% p99 delta
- 2025-01-13 11:00 - gamma bisect started (mid-size commit window)

Notes to self / communication guidance for on-call: keep message succinct: what we saw, what we changed (if anything), immediate mitigation, next steps, and ETA for follow-up. Example slack blurb:
  "On-call: p99 latency for model-x-route drifted ~+100ms over last week. Root-candidate: batching heuristic change (PR#456). Rolling back candidate or applying per-route batch_timeout override is top mitigation. Running perf-bisect now, will update with results in ~3h. Aisha, Miguel, Zoe on it."

Attachments to include when closing incident: perf-harness artifacts (JSON), flamegraphs, Grafana snapshots (before/after), git SHAs, rollout IDs, and a short postmortem paragraph summarizing cause and permanent fix planned.

If you get stuck: ping eng-platform (infra) to rule out driver/kernel rollouts; ping model-ops to confirm no model/regeneration happened.

End of notes.
